extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of philosophy, aesthetics, and humor theory
extracted.subtask_description: A scholarly philosophical account of the comical explaining the origin and nature of laughter in terms of the relation between abstract concepts and intuitive particulars. The chapter situates Schopenhauer's theory relative to earlier attempts (Cicero, Hutcheson, Kant, Jean Paul).

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition between intuitive and abstract representations
rubrics_metrics.description: My theory of the comical is also based on the opposition between intuitive and abstract representations that I laid such particular emphasis on in the previous chapters;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schopenhauer frames the comical in terms of a fundamental cognitive opposition: 'intuitive' (concrete, perceptual particulars) versus 'abstract' (conceptual generalizations). The explanation of laughter depends on this distinction and refers back to prior chapters where the distinction is developed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comical arises from paradoxical/unexpected subsumption
rubrics_metrics.description: the comical always comes from a paradoxical and therefore unexpected subsumption of some subject matter under a concept that is, however, different from it,
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Laughter is produced when a subject matter is (unexpectedly) forced under an inappropriate or incongruent concept — a paradoxical classification. The key mechanism is a sudden, surprising mapping between concept and subject that does not fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sudden perception of incongruity between concept and real subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: the phenomenon of laughter always signifies the sudden perception of an incongruity between a concept and the real subject matter that is thought through it, and thus between the abstract and the intuitive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schopenhauer identifies the psychological event causing laughter as the instantaneous recognition of mismatch: one apprehends a concept (abstract) being applied to a particular (intuitive) in a way that reveals their incompatibility. This incongruity (abstract vs. intuitive) is the central explanatory principle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magnitude and unexpectedness of incongruity determine laughter intensity
rubrics_metrics.description: The greater and more unexpected the incongruity is to the person who is laughing, the more uproarious his laughter will be.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a graded or scalar account: both the size of the mismatch and the degree to which it surprises the perceiver increase the force/volume of laughter. Unexpectedness is an essential modifier of the comic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Every comic instance involves a concept and a particular that can be (mis)subsumed
rubrics_metrics.description: with everything that causes laughter there will always prove to be a concept and a particular, which is to say a thing or event that certainly can be subsumed under this concept and therefore thought through it, but nevertheless does not remotely belong there in any other or more pertinent respect, and is clearly different from everything else that is thought through this concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical diagnostic: to analyze a comic event, identify (a) the general concept invoked and (b) the particular that is being (improperly) subsumed under it. The particular must be formally classifiable under the concept yet markedly inappropriate in relevant respects — that tension produces the comic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumption of a universal, single-origin for laughter
rubrics_metrics.description: The problem of the origin of laughter (an origin that is everywhere the same) and its proper meaning was already recognized by Cicero, ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schopenhauer treats the origin of laughter as a uniform psychological phenomenon across contexts; the theory aims to give a single explanatory mechanism (incongruity between abstract concept and intuitive particular) rather than multiple context-specific explanations.
